core_obligations: Sharpen Q: a germ with Q has arbitrarily small representatives with P (proof lines 8086-8090).
Take a diagram of germs as in the definition and choose representatives U_1 -> V of h and an etale representative b_1 : V'_1 -> V of b (proof lines 8091-8100).
Choose representatives a_1 and h'_1 with a_1 etale, and shrink U'_1 to make the square commute (proof lines 8101-8103).
Reduce the claim to the equivalence u' in W(h'_1) iff u in W(h_1) and apply the etale-etale locality lemma (proof lines 8104-8107).
proof_roadmap: Choice of representatives in the germ diagram (proof lines 8091-8103).
Reduction to the W-equivalence and conclusion (proof lines 8104-8107).
difficulty_reason: Given a property P of morphisms of schemes that is etale local on the source-and-target, the lemma asserts that the property Q of morphisms of germs defined by the existence of a representative with P is itself etale local on the source-and-target (statement lines 8069-8083). The proof first sharpens the hypothesis: a germ with Q has arbitrarily small neighbourhoods U, V such that a representative U -> V has P, which follows from the chapter's implication lemma; then it takes a diagram of germs as in the definition, chooses representatives U_1 -> V, an etale representative b_1 : V'_1 -> V, and representatives a_1, h'_1 with a_1 etale, shrinks U'_1 so that the square commutes, and observes that by the initial remark the goal is exactly the equivalence u' in W(h'_1) iff u in W(h_1), which is the content of the etale-etale locality lemma (proof lines 8085-8107). The level is H3: the reduction to prescribed representatives of the germs is the delicate step and every choice (representative, etale representative, shrinking) is made explicitly.
